pm_exper_user_2528_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.question: How can I stay motivated when my efforts to inspire people don’t seem to be making a difference?
pm_exper_user_2528_maasv_v0446_pmv2_r1.all_options:
(a) When declining student engagement makes it difficult to stay energised, remember that the cultural groundwork you’ve sown on campus may bear fruit later, even if it’s not immediately visible. Drawing on your appreciation for traditional cultural displays, you could co-create moments with students that blend heritage with contemporary relevance, giving both you and them a renewed sense of connection.
(b) When it feels like your efforts aren’t making an impact, try to focus on the small but positive moments you can find in your work. Taking time to reflect on what you can control and to connect with people who do appreciate your efforts can help keep your motivation steady.
(c) When waning student engagement leaves you disheartened, it can help to focus on the individual moments where your investment in campus culture has sparked connection, even if attendance numbers look modest. Revisiting these small wins and inviting candid dialogue with a handful of engaged students can restore clarity about the deeper purpose behind your efforts.
(d) If diminished participation in campus activities is wearing on your motivation, try centring your attention on the tangible, personal impacts your work has had—those quieter successes that don’t always appear in metrics. Bringing a few committed student leaders into conversation about what resonates most for them can reignite your own sense of purpose.
